question:
A 27-year-old male with a history of poorly controlled HIV, chronic hepatitis C, and active intravenous
heroin use (last use 2 days ago) comes to the emergency department with progressive right-sided back
pain over several weeks. The pain extends to his thigh and knee, with no recent trauma reported. His
vital signs show a temperature of 37.4°C (99.4°F), blood pressure of 122/71 mmHg, and pulse of
120/min. Physical examination reveals pain on passive right leg extension and an antalgic gait, but no
focal back tenderness, step-offs, or deformities. Neurovascular examination of both lower extremities is
unremarkable, and the patient has normal urination. What complication is this patient most likely to
develop if left untreated? Answer Choices: (A) Pyogenic liver abscess (B) Bilateral lower extremity
paraplegia (C) Cauda equina syndrome (D) Retroperitoneal hemorrhage (E) Sciatic nerve compression
(F) Rectus sheath hematoma (G) Diverticulum perforation (H) Femoral neuropathy (I) Septic arthritis of

the hip (J) Epidural abscess formation
 A. Femoral neuropathy
B. Septic arthritis of the hip
C. Sciatic nerve compression
D. Epidural abscess formation
E. Retroperitoneal hemorrhage
F. Pyogenic liver abscess
G. Cauda equina syndrome
H. Bilateral lower extremity paraplegia
I. Rectus sheath hematoma
J. Diverticulum perforation
